mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE < 5% does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening demand for housing and broader economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO MoM < -2% does not correlate with subsequent supply shocks.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of FEDFUNDS > 4% and rising CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS MoM > 300,000 does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 5% year-over-year and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 6%, it signals strong consumer demand and a healthy labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: strong consumer demand and healthy labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of RSAFS YoY > 5% and UNRATE < 6% does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month, coupled with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5%, signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of INDPRO MoM < -1% and UNRATE MoM > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic downturns.
